title: Given a Scenario, Troubleshoot Common Issues with Network Services

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A physical link can be healthy while switching, filtering, routing, or addressing still prevents service. Use the symptom's scope to locate the failing layer.
bullets: Incorrect VLAN assignment and ACL behavior
Gateway, IP address, duplicate-address, and subnet-mask errors
sections.callout: CHECK SWITCHING → CHECK VLAN → CHECK FILTERING → CHECK ROUTING → CHECK ADDRESSING

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Determine whether the failure affects a switched path, a logical segment, an allowed flow, a routed destination, or the host's own address configuration.
bullets: Broadcast storm or unstable MAC learning → STP loop
User placed in the wrong subnet → Incorrect VLAN
Unknown remote network → Routing table or default route
Clients cannot receive leases → Address pool exhaustion
Local works but remote fails → Default gateway or route

entries.title: Network Loops
paragraphs: Redundant Layer 2 links without correct STP control can circulate frames indefinitely, causing broadcast storms, duplicate frames, and unstable MAC tables.

entries.title: Root Bridge Selection
paragraphs: STP builds its topology around the root bridge. An unintended root can force inefficient paths and unpredictable forwarding decisions.

entries.title: Port Roles
paragraphs: Roles describe each port's job in the spanning-tree topology, such as root, designated, or alternate.

entries.title: Port States
paragraphs: States describe whether a port is learning or forwarding traffic. A port held in a nonforwarding state may be working exactly as STP intends—or may reveal a topology issue.
entries.memoryHook: State = what the port is doing now.

entries.title: Incorrect VLAN Assignment
paragraphs: A device assigned to the wrong VLAN joins the wrong broadcast domain and usually receives or expects addressing for the wrong subnet.

entries.title: Access Control List (ACL)
paragraphs: An ACL with the wrong address, protocol, port, direction, order, or implicit deny can block otherwise valid traffic.
entries.memoryHook: If a specific flow fails, inspect the rule path.

entries.title: Routing Table
paragraphs: The routing table must contain a valid path for the destination. A missing, stale, or less-preferred entry can send traffic incorrectly or leave it unroutable.

entries.title: Default Route
paragraphs: The default route carries traffic when no more-specific route exists. If it is absent or points to the wrong next hop, unknown remote destinations fail.
entries.memoryHook: No specific match → use the default.

entries.title: Address Pool Exhaustion
paragraphs: When a DHCP scope has no available leases, new clients cannot obtain valid configuration.
entries.memoryHook: Existing clients may work while new clients fail.

entries.title: Incorrect Default Gateway
paragraphs: A host can reach its local subnet but cannot reach remote networks when its gateway is missing or wrong.

entries.title: Incorrect IP Address
paragraphs: An address outside the intended subnet or VLAN prevents normal communication.

entries.title: Duplicate IP Address
paragraphs: Two hosts using the same address produce intermittent reachability, address-conflict messages, and changing ARP mappings.

entries.title: Incorrect Subnet Mask
paragraphs: The mask tells a host which destinations are local. A wrong mask makes the host send traffic to the wrong place—or skip the gateway when it is required.
entries.memoryHook: The mask defines local versus remote.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Broadcast storm and MAC flapping → STP loop
Unexpected spanning-tree path → Root bridge selection
Particular protocol or destination blocked → ACL
Specific destination has no path → Routing table
All unknown networks fail → Default route
New clients lack leases → Address pool exhaustion
Local subnet works but remote does not → Default gateway
Host misjudges local network → Subnet mask

entries.title: STP Loop vs. Wrong VLAN
paragraphs: A loop produces widespread Layer 2 instability; a wrong VLAN isolates or misplaces a specific device or port.

entries.title: Port Role vs. Port State
paragraphs: Role is the port's topology function; state describes its current forwarding behavior.

entries.title: Routing Table vs. Default Route
paragraphs: The routing table contains all known routes; the default is the fallback when no specific match exists.

entries.title: Gateway vs. IP Address
paragraphs: A bad gateway commonly preserves local access but breaks remote access. A bad IP may break local communication too.

entries.title: Gateway vs. Subnet Mask
paragraphs: The gateway forwards remote traffic; the mask decides which traffic is remote.

entries.title: Pool Exhaustion vs. Duplicate IP
paragraphs: Exhaustion denies new leases. A duplicate creates conflicting ownership and intermittent connectivity.

entries.title: ACL vs. Route
paragraphs: An ACL denies a flow by policy. A routing problem means the network lacks or chooses the wrong path.
